reason: A presents a complete, cohesive design system — branded identity (logo, wordmark, tracked micro-labels), a 72px/800 hero with a restrained gradient accent word, a pulsing live-status card, and a 4-up telemetry grid with 48px counters on a subtle gradient/starfield background — with consistent radii (20-24px), spacing, and typographic hierarchy throughout. B is competent and professional (clean minimal template, incident cards, per-service sparklines) but reads as a stock SaaS status page with no design voice, and it clips its own GitHub nav item at the right edge on 390px mobile. A's mobile is flawless by comparison — single column, 2-up metric grid, no overflow, consistent language across viewports — so A wins on both desktop showpiece impact and desktop/mobile consistency.
gap: A lacks the per-service uptime history visualisation that is B's strongest asset (Google/Wikipedia rows with uptime %, response time, and green area sparklines) — beneath the telemetry counters, add an animated uptime/response chart row so the page communicates real monitored data, not just aggregate stats.
